 Ipsita Pati / Nov 16, 2026, 00:28 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Gurgaon: India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast shallow to moderate fog at isolated places across Haryana during night and morning hours from Monday. The forecast comes after foggy conditions were witnessed in parts of the city on Sunday morning, with visibility dropping in some areas. The city’s minimum temperature rose to 16.4°C, up 2.4°C from the previous 24 hours. IMD has forecast a fall of 3-4°C in minimum temperatures across Haryana over the next 24 hours, signalling a change towards cooler night conditions. In its seven-day weather bulletin issued on Sunday, IMD forecast light to moderate rainfall at isolated places in the city, Faridabad, Nuh, Palwal, Jhajjar, Rohtak, Sonipat, Panipat, Jind, Chandigarh, Panchkula, Ambala, Yamunanagar, Kurukshetra and Kaithal on Nov 16. However, the weather is likely to remain dry across the state from Nov 17 to Nov 21. The bulletin attributed the prevailing weather system to a western disturbance, which persists as a cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan and neighbouring areas, with an associated trough in the middle tropospheric westerlies.  Across Haryana, the average minimum temperature rose by 1.3°C compared with Saturday, but remained 4°C above normal on Sunday. Bhiwani recorded the lowest minimum temperature in the state at 14°C. Among other stations, Karnal recorded 14.2°C, Fatehabad 14.3°C and Sirsa 15.7°C. The state’s highest maximum temperature was recorded at 29.9°C in Chandigarh. IMD reported no large change in maximum temperatures, which remained within the normal range. Very light rainfall occurred at isolated places in Haryana during the preceding 24 hours, but no station recorded significant rainfall exceeding 1 cm. The department has not issued any weather warning for Haryana during the next seven days, with dry conditions expected to prevail after Sunday’s isolated rainfall forecast.
